result_summary: Norm-mass marginals produce no effect on the ibm 11-summary panel: d' 4.684 to 4.673 (delta -0.011) against a predicted +0.2 to +0.8 gain, margin +4.708 to +4.720 closeness pts (delta +0.012), R 1.6697 to 1.6679, DR 0.08728 to 0.08720, largest per-document distance change +0.00148, ranking unchanged. The bar reads met literally (V 0/24, margin +4.720 >= +4.58, d' 4.673 >= 4.60, identity smd 0.0, order_gap bit-identical), but the harness's own uniform baseline already clears those absolute thresholds, so the bar does not separate the lever from doing nothing. The cause is visible in the gate that passed it: the pooled norm CV 0.0446 cleared the 0.03 death line, yet the mass vector is a within-document object whose per-document CV median is 0.0198, giving mass vectors 0.0001 to 0.0141 in total variation from uniform and a heaviest statement at 1.084x its uniform share - and two of the four adversarial documents segment to 1 and 3 statements, so their masses are uniform by construction. The premise survives, only the magnitude fails: corr(norm, token count) is -0.1597, so the discarded norm is a genuine content signal and not statement length, but mmBERT statement norms (mean 30.17, sd 1.35) are too concentrated to reshape an exact EMD.
caveats: Single fixture, in-sample: the 11 ibm-ai-adoption summaries that set the calibration are the same 11 that score it, and the null result is a statement about this corpus's norm spread (4.5% pooled, 2.0% within-document), not a general refutation of norm-scaled mass. Two adversarial fixtures carry 1 and 3 statements, so the lever has almost no purchase on the adversarial side of the boundary the margin measures - a wider or better-segmented adversarial tier could change the reading. The acceptance bar's absolute thresholds (+4.58, 4.60) come from the E01 torch bf16 GPU row while this run uses the shipped OpenVINO INT8 encoder on CPU, which reproduces that row within 2.80%; the bar is therefore recorded as met while the verdict follows the delta over the co-measured baseline. The latency reading 0.877x is not a measurement - the 64-thread CPU was shared with concurrent campaign executors; the defensible claim is only that the weights cost nothing, as predicted. The registered second stage (feeding the same masses to the OPW order axis) was not run, correctly, since it was conditioned on the semantic axis passing; it would inherit the same near-uniform mass vectors.
